run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-17T11:02:12Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for otel-demo/frontend is explained by the otel-demo product-catalog Deployment: its revision-2 pod template sets the container command to ["invalid-command"], so the container never starts. Metric evidence shows frontend span errors were zero through 11:01 and then rose sharply (516.7 per 5m at 11:02, 4469 at 11:04, 6010 at 11:05), with frontend's own error spans concentrated on grpc client calls to ProductCatalogService/GetProduct, RecommendationService/ListRecommendations and CheckoutService/PlaceOrder plus tcp.connect failures. Kubernetes evidence shows ReplicaSet product-catalog-fcf7564cf created at 11:00:21 with command ["invalid-command"] (the earlier revision-1 ReplicaSet product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc has no command and the same image), the old pod killed at 11:00:30, and pod product-catalog-fcf7564cf-vjj7l stuck in CrashLoopBackOff with restartCount 5 and last termination reason StartError, exit code 128, message exec: "invalid-command": executable file not found in $PATH. The product-catalog Service has no ready endpoints, and product-catalog's server-side span volume fell from 3694.4 per 5m at 11:00 to 888.9 at 11:05. Frontend-proxy, checkout and recommendation show their own error spans over the same interval; accounting, payment and fraud-detection error series stayed at zero. Hypotheses rejected: flagd fault injection (productCatalogFailure defaultVariant is "off") and the earlier fraud-detection OOMKill (10:50:24, zero error spans). Who or what applied the product-catalog Deployment change could not be determined; change history is not an available integration.

claims.text: Frontend span errors were absent before the incident and appeared around 11:00-11:02: sum(increase(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])) returned 0 at every point from 10:25 through 11:01, then 516.67 at 11:02, 499.03 at 11:03, 4469.05 at 11:04 and 6010.47 at 11:05.

At 1-minute resolution the first non-zero frontend error increase is 930 error spans in the window ending 11:01:45, after zero values back through 10:59:00; frontend-proxy shows the same onset pattern (1446 in that 1m window).

Frontend's error spans by operation at 11:04/11:05 include client spans grpc.oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct (809.27/1097.12), grpc.oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations (149.30/204.14), grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder (114.44/144.44), plus server spans GET (1123.33/1514.44), POST (114.44/144.44) and tcp.connect (12.22/14.44 per 5m).

Error spans in the same interval are also present on the services frontend calls: frontend-proxy's own error spans rose from 804.44 per 5m at 11:02 to 3332.22 at 11:05, recommendation's own get_product_list//oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/ListProducts error spans were 153.48 at 11:04 and 204.14 at 11:05, and checkout's own oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder and oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct error spans were 96.28 at 11:04 and 120.23 at 11:05.

product-catalog's server-side span volume collapsed over the incident window: oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct fell from 3694.44 spans per 5m at 11:00 to 888.89 at 11:05 and oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/ListProducts from 312.22 to 73.33, while product-catalog emitted no STATUS_CODE_ERROR span series in that window.

The otel-demo Deployment product-catalog (Helm release otel-demo, revision 2, observedGeneration 4) currently defines container command ["invalid-command"] for image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-product-catalog, and its status reports Available=False reason MinimumReplicasUnavailable, replicas 1, unavailableReplicas 1, and the condition message "Deployment does not have minimum availability."

Ownership chain: ReplicaSet product-catalog-fcf7564cf (owner Deployment product-catalog, deployment revision 2, created 2026-11-17T11:00:21Z, replicas 1) carries container command ["invalid-command"], while the earlier ReplicaSet product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc (deployment revision 1, created 2026-11-17T10:30:20Z, replicas 0) has command null for the same image tag ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-product-catalog.

Pod product-catalog-fcf7564cf-vjj7l (owner ReplicaSet product-catalog-fcf7564cf) is in phase Running but not ready (Ready=False, ContainersNotReady) with restartCount 5 and container state waiting reason CrashLoopBackOff ("back-off 2m40s restarting failed container"); its last termination has reason StartError, exitCode 128 and message "failed to create containerd task: failed to create shim task: OCI runtime create failed: runc create failed: unable to start container process: error during container init: exec: \"invalid-command\": executable file not found in $PATH".

Events in otel-demo tie the rollout and failures to the incident window: Deployment product-catalog ScalingReplicaSet "Scaled down replica set product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc from 1 to 0" at 11:00:30 and "Scaled up replica set product-catalog-fcf7564cf from 0 to 1" at 11:00:38; pod product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-wzpwm Killing at 11:00:30; ReplicaSet product-catalog-fcf7564cf SuccessfulCreate at 11:00:21 and 11:00:38; Pod Failed with the exec "invalid-command" error at 11:00:26 and 11:03:51 and 25 BackOff events on pod product-catalog-fcf7564cf-vjj7l.

The product-catalog Service has no ready endpoints: the Endpoints object product-catalog lists only notReadyAddresses (ip 100.96.2.148, targetRef Pod product-catalog-fcf7564cf-vjj7l) on port tcp-service 8080.

Across all 21 otel-demo Deployments, product-catalog is the only one whose container declares a non-null command (["invalid-command"]); every other Deployment reported available=1 and ready=1, while product-catalog reported available=null and ready=null.

Error signals of other services were checked: accounting, payment and fraud-detection returned STATUS_CODE_ERROR series that were 0 throughout 11:00-11:05, and ad returned 1.11 error spans per 5m at 11:00 and 11:01 (present before the frontend deviation) and 0 afterwards.
The flagd-config ConfigMap's demo.flagd.json shows all 12 flags (including productCatalogFailure, cartFailure, paymentFailure, recommendationCacheFailure) with state ENABLED and defaultVariant "off".

A separate container restart occurred earlier in the window: fraud-detection pod fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-8bpr4 has restartCount 1 with last termination reason OOMKilled, exitCode 137 at 10:50:24Z, and its container has been running since 10:50:24Z.

product-catalog produced no error-status spans of its own (its GetProduct/ListProducts series carry only STATUS_CODE_UNSET); the failure observed for it is a container-start failure, not application-level error responses, so the absence of its own error spans does not indicate health.

flagd-driven product-catalog failure (productCatalogFailure fault flag) was considered and rejected as this cause: the flag exists but its configured defaultVariant is "off", and the observed failure is the container exec of "invalid-command" declared in the Deployment, not a flag-injected application fault.

The fraud-detection OOMKill at 10:50:24Z was considered as a contributor and rejected: it occurred about ten minutes before the frontend error deviation and fraud-detection's own error-span series stayed at 0 through 11:00-11:05.

The frontend request errors are caused by product-catalog having no ready endpoints after the 11:00:21-11:00:38 rollout: callers of ProductCatalogService (frontend, recommendation, checkout) fail on the grpc client spans/tcp.connect while product-catalog cannot serve, and frontend surfaces these as GET/POST request errors; identifying the actor that applied the Deployment change would require change history.

Restore the product-catalog Deployment pod template to the revision-1 form (no command override, container command/entrypoint taken from image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-product-catalog) so the container starts, and verify the new pod reaches Ready and that the product-catalog Endpoints object gains ready addresses.

Review the source of the otel-demo Helm release values/CI change that produced Deployment product-catalog revision 2 with command ["invalid-command"], and watch frontend error rate plus grpc.oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct error spans after the rollback.

gaps: Who or what applied Deployment otel-demo/product-catalog revision 2 (command ["invalid-command"]) at 11:00:21-11:00:38Z is unknown: the change_history integration is not available in this Run and Helm release data is stored in secrets that cannot be read.

Jaeger trace detail during the incident is missing: a trace search for product-catalog over 11:00-11:05 returned no traces, and the frontend trace search over 10:40-11:05 reported source samples only up to 10:45:39Z, so incident-time trace error details (status messages on frontend client spans) could not be read.

Application logs could not be used: fetch_pod_logs for frontend-675fd7b5c5-9f6l5 (10:59-11:11) and product-catalog-fcf7564cf-vjj7l (11:00-11:11) returned 0 lines, so no runtime error text from either container is available.

The alerting rule RequestErrorRate is not present in this Prometheus: list_prometheus_rules filtered by rule_name RequestErrorRate and by type=alert both returned nothing, so the exact alert expression and its 16.87 value could not be verified.

Error state of cart, currency, email, shipping, image-provider and quote is unknown: the service-level error-span query returned series only for accounting, ad, checkout, fraud-detection, frontend, frontend-proxy, payment and recommendation, and a missing series is unknown rather than zero.

NetworkPolicies, ResourceQuotas and the Service selector/spec were not inspected in this Run; the observed fault mechanism (container start failure with no ready endpoints) was sufficient, but these were not verified.

Kubernetes objects were read at 11:12, after the authorized window end (11:11:44); their earlier state is not directly observed, and timing statements rely on object creationTimestamp values and events timestamped inside the window.
next_steps: Roll back Deployment otel-demo/product-catalog to revision 1 (remove the ["invalid-command"] command override) and confirm pod readiness plus ready Endpoints for Service product-catalog.
Trace the origin of the Helm values/CI change that set command: ["invalid-command"] on the product-catalog container, using Helm release history or the change-history integration when available.
After remediation, re-check frontend STATUS_CODE_ERROR span rate and the ProductCatalogService/GetProduct error series until they return to the pre-11:00 baseline of zero.
Review the separate fraud-detection OOMKill (exit 137 at 10:50:24Z) on its own, since it is unrelated to this alert but is a real container restart.

Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind.
